1. Liability of Newness 
• What it Means: New businesses often fail because they lack a proven track record, and 
their members struggle to adapt to new roles. 
• Why It’s a Problem:  
o Team members may not fully understand the challenges of operating a new 
venture. 
o The lack of established business processes makes operations inefficient. 
• How to Overcome It:  
o Assemble a skilled management team with experience in startups or the industry.

• How to Overcome It:  
o Assemble a skilled management team with experience in startups or the industry. 
o Build credibility and gain early trust from stakeholders like customers, partners, 
and investors. 
 
2. New-Venture Team 
• Definition: The team includes founders, employees, and advisors who drive the business 
from concept to a fully functioning firm. 
• Key Points:  
o The team evolves over time as the company grows and can afford to add 
members.

• Key Points:  
o The team evolves over time as the company grows and can afford to add 
members. 
o It includes more than just paid employees. Boards of directors, advisors, and 
external professionals are part of this team. 
 
3. Founding Team 
• Founders’ Influence: The founders’ skills, decisions, and leadership directly shape the 
company’s culture and growth path. 
• Team Size:  
o Studies show that 50%-70% of new ventures are started by multiple founders.

• Team Size:  
o Studies show that 50%-70% of new ventures are started by multiple founders. 
o Teams bring diversity in expertise but can also face conflicts. 
• Advantages:  
o More skills and ideas. 
o Wider social and professional networks for support and growth. 
o Emotional and psychological backing among cofounders. 
• Disadvantages:  
o Team members may disagree on critical decisions. 
o Conflicts can arise over leadership roles and work habits.

o Team members may disagree on critical decisions. 
o Conflicts can arise over leadership roles and work habits. 
o Duplication of skills can limit the breadth of expertise.

4. Key Attributes of a Strong Team 
• Diversity: Teams with varied skills and backgrounds are more effective than 
homogeneous ones. 
• Education: Higher education enhances problem-solving and entrepreneurial skills. 
• Experience:  
o Prior entrepreneurial experience helps avoid costly mistakes. 
o Industry experience improves networking, marketing, and management 
capabilities. 
• Networking:  
o Broad professional and social networks allow access to capital, know-how, and 
referrals.

• Networking:  
o Broad professional and social networks allow access to capital, know-how, and 
referrals. 
 
5. Recruiting and Selecting Employees 
• Tailored Recruitment:  
o Startups may operate with founders initially, adding employees as needed. 
o A skills profile helps identify gaps and prioritize recruitment. 
• Sources of Labor:  
o Full/Part-Time Employees: Work on-site using company tools and policies. 
o Interns: Offer fresh talent at a lower cost while gaining experience.

o Interns: Offer fresh talent at a lower cost while gaining experience. 
o Freelancers: Flexible, project-based workers who bring expertise. 
o Virtual Assistants: Remote professionals offering administrative or technical 
support. 
 
6. Board of Directors 
• Role:  
o Legally required for corporations. 
o Members oversee management and strategic direction. 
• Responsibilities:  
o Appoint officers of the company. 
o Declare dividends. 
o Monitor corporate affairs. 
• Value to Startups:

o Appoint officers of the company. 
o Declare dividends. 
o Monitor corporate affairs. 
• Value to Startups:  
o Provides legitimacy to attract investors and customers. 
o Offers strategic guidance and industry connections. 
 
7. Board of Advisors

• What It Is:  
o A nonbinding, advisory panel that helps management with decisions. 
o Unlike the board of directors, it has no legal responsibilities. 
• Benefits:  
o Easier to attract members due to lower commitment and no legal liability. 
o Enhances credibility and provides targeted advice. 
• Best Practices:  
o Ensure meaningful roles to avoid disillusionment. 
o Select advisors with complementary skills. 
o Define confidentiality rules clearly. 
 
8. Lenders and Investors

o Select advisors with complementary skills. 
o Define confidentiality rules clearly. 
 
8. Lenders and Investors 
• Contributions:  
o Provide funding and help recruit key team members. 
o Offer insights into target markets and business strategies. 
o Help establish partnerships and fine-tune the business model. 
• Added Value:  
o Introduce the firm to additional sources of capital. 
o Act as a stabilizing force during uncertainties. 
 
9. Other Professionals 
• Key Players:

o Act as a stabilizing force during uncertainties. 
 
9. Other Professionals 
• Key Players:  
o Attorneys ensure legal compliance and protect intellectual property. 
o Accountants manage financial records and tax obligations. 
o Business consultants advise on strategy and operations. 
• Types of Consultants:  
o Paid consultants offer specialized expertise. 
o Nonprofit/government-supported consultants provide affordable guidance.

o Nonprofit/government-supported consultants provide affordable guidance. 
 
These points create a comprehensive view of building a new-venture team, with strategies to 
overcome challenges and maximize the strengths of diverse team members. Let me know if 
you'd like an even deeper dive into any specific area!
